You've never even seen it? Are you somewhere other than the US (if you are, you should know that cornmeal is what is sold in some other countries as polenta. It is NOT cornflour, which is called corn starch in the US, and is a totally different thing from cornmeal, which is basically finely ground corn.)

Preheat oven to 450F

1 1/2 C cornmeal (if you have access to white cornmeal, use it!! If not it's still very good with yellow.)

3 Tbsp flour

1 tsp salt

1 tsp baking soda

2 C buttermilk (can use sour cream if you don't have buttermilk, but buttermilk is better)

1 egg

2 Tbsp butter and/or bacon fat, melted

1 Tbsp bacon fat, lard, beef drippings, or shortening for the pan.

Place the 1 Tbsp of bacon fat into a round 9 or 10 inch pan or cast iron skillet. Place into the preheated oven to melt and heat up while you mix the ingredients. It should be in the oven about 10 minutes--so do not use butter for this part, because it will burn.

Sift dry ingredients together in one bowl. In other mix the buttermilk and egg, and then stir in the melted butter/butter and fat mix. The butter may re-solidify into small lumps when mixed in, that's okay.

Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir until it's just mixed and moist and there are no big streaks or clumps of dry cornmeal left. The mixture will be a bit lumpy; you want that. Do not mix until smooth!

Pour the mixture into the preheated pan. Be careful--it will sizzle quite a bit, and the edges of the mixture will already begin to puff up from it. Some of the fat may end up on top of the batter, which is also fine.

Bake 20 - 25 minutes--it's done when the center bounces back or a toothpick comes out clean or with just a few damp crumbs.

I like to drop a splodge of butter on top of it when it's come out of the oven and smear it around to cover the entire top. The butter melts into the bread a little. This cornbread definitely benefits from butter IMO (but then IMO all cornbreads do), but plenty of people like it plain, too.

The only thing that isn't amazing about this recipe is it's not great as cold leftovers. It reheats just fine, but it's just not as good cold (which a lot of cornbreads are). This is a true Southern cornbread, without much wheat flour and no sugar, whereas Yankee cornbreads have a lot more flour and usually include sugar as well. That means this isn't as soft and squishy as a Yankee cornbread, either. The good news is, if you're cooking for more than four people you might very well not have any leftovers anyway. :-)

Enjoy! If you make it, let me know how it turned out and what you think of it!
